Joint bivariate family with negative-binomial components for partially observed pairs

Source: R/binegbin.R
binegbin_partialobs.Rd

Returns a version of binegbin() for partially paired designs, in which source 1 has missing values. The generative model, family name, dpars, and post-processing methods are the same as for binegbin(). Each row also supplies an observation indicator as the second argument of vint(), after y2:

brm(
  bf(y1 | vint(y2, y1_obs) ~ ...),
  family   = binegbin_partialobs(),
  stanvars = binegbin_partialobs_stanvars(),
  data     = dat
)

This template is for the native parameterisation. To fit the model in the congruence–bias parameterisation, which we recommend, write the formula with bf_mfd().

y1_obs is 1 on rows where both counts were recorded and 0 on rows where only y2 was recorded. An indicator other than 0 or 1 makes the sampler fail at initialisation, with a message in the chain output that names the cause. The check also catches the two vint() arguments written in reverse order.

Do not use NA for missing y1 values. brms drops any row with a missing response with only a warning. On a row with y1_obs == 0, the likelihood term does not depend on y1, so y1 can be any integer. We suggest -1, because it cannot be confused with a recorded count:

dat$y1[dat$y1_obs == 0] <- -1L

Usage

binegbin_partialobs()

binegbin_partialobs_stanvars()

Value

binegbin_partialobs() returns a brms custom_family object. binegbin_partialobs_stanvars() returns a stanvars object holding the Stan code for the corresponding _lpmf. The returned family has the same name as binegbin(), so the post-processing methods documented there apply to a fit made with either constructor.

Details

On a paired row, the likelihood term is the joint probability of (y1, y2) under binegbin(). On an unpaired row, the likelihood term is the marginal probability of y2, the joint probability summed over every possible value of the unrecorded y1: P(y2) = sum_k NB2(k | mu, shapes) NB2(y2 - k | lambdatwo, shapextwo) over k = 0, ..., y2.

To impute y1 on the unpaired rows, use posterior_predict_y1_given_y2() or posterior_epred_y1_given_y2(); see vignette("prediction").

lambdaone and shapexone do not appear in the likelihood term for an unpaired row, so lambdaone and shapexone are estimated from the paired rows alone. With few paired rows, the posteriors of lambdaone and shapexone are wide and depend strongly on their priors. mu, shapes, lambdatwo, and shapextwo appear in both likelihood terms and are informed by every row.

See also

binegbin() for the fully paired case; bipois_partialobs() for the equidispersed Poisson counterpart.
